title: Classical Books and Influential Thinkers — First Topic Pool
purpose: Generate original mindset-first lessons inspired by books and speakers. This file is an editorial pool, not an instruction to produce or publish videos.

copyright_rules.modern_books_and_speeches: Paraphrase ideas in original wording; do not reproduce distinctive passages.
copyright_rules.direct_quotes: Do not use unless public-domain status, permission, or a suitable licence is documented. Attribution alone is not permission.
copyright_rules.attribution: Verify the author and originating work. Describe an idea as inspiration rather than presenting an unverified paraphrase as a direct quotation.
copyright_rules.claim_review: Verify factual claims independently; a book reference is not evidence that every claim in a script is accurate.

topics.title: Why You Should Pay Yourself First
topics.original_lesson: Build a saving habit by deliberately setting aside a realistic amount when income arrives, rather than relying only on whatever remains.
topics.notes: Existing topics discuss postponing saving and small repeatable habits; this candidate focuses specifically on prioritising saving at the point income arrives.

topics.title: Looking Rich Is Not the Same as Being Wealthy
topics.original_lesson: Visible spending does not reveal a person's financial security or full circumstances.

topics.title: Your Financial Future Begins With What You Believe Is Possible
topics.original_lesson: Beliefs can influence which financial goals people consider and whether they seek knowledge or take constructive steps.
topics.notes: Avoid presenting positive thinking as a guarantee of wealth or as a substitute for structural realities and practical action.

topics.title: Small Money Habits Can Shape Your Financial Future
topics.original_lesson: Repeated everyday choices can reinforce a financial habit over time.

topics.title: Stop Competing With Other People's Money
topics.original_lesson: Do not use another person's visible lifestyle as the measure of your own financial progress.

topics.title: Motivation Won't Save You Without Discipline
topics.original_lesson: A financial goal needs repeatable actions and routines; motivation alone is unreliable.
topics.notes: Use an independently verified Zig Ziglar source if his ideas are referenced. Do not attribute a circulating quote without locating its original source.

topics.title: Every Purchase Costs More Than Money
topics.original_lesson: Consider the time, energy and trade-offs involved in earning the money used for a purchase.
topics.notes: This introduces the specific time-and-life-energy lens rather than repeating general spending awareness.

topics.title: The Danger of Wanting to Get Rich Quickly
topics.original_lesson: Impatience and unrealistic expectations can weaken judgement and increase vulnerability to reckless offers and scams.

topics.title: Stop Living Only for Today

inspiration.work: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
inspiration.author: Stephen R. Covey

topics.original_lesson: Bring future priorities into today's choices without ignoring present needs.

topics.title: Never Underestimate the Power of Consistency
topics.original_lesson: Small repeatable actions can be more sustainable than waiting for perfect conditions or relying on bursts of motivation.

summary.reason_not_auto_added: Candidates require editorial approval and source/claim review before entering the production topic library.
